written.myAnswer: In yeast, a small outgrowth called a bud forms on the parent cell. The bud grows and may separate from the parent or remain attached.
Fungi produce spores, often in sporangia. When mature, the sporangium releases the spores. In favourable conditions, the spores germinate and grow into new fungi.

Fungal spores have thick walls that help them survive unfavourable conditions; they germinate when conditions become favourable. Bacterial endospores can survive harsh conditions, even after the original cell dies, and can develop into bacteria when conditions improve.
A runner, or stolon, is a horizontal stem that grows above the ground. Roots and shoots develop at its nodes, forming new plants. Strawberry plants reproduce by runners.
A potato tuber is a fleshy underground stem. Its eyes are buds that can sprout and grow into new plants.

Asexual reproduction occurs without fusion of gametes and usually produces offspring genetically identical to the parent. Sexual reproduction involves fusion of male and female gametes and produces offspring with variation.

In bacteria, the DNA replicates, the cell elongates, and the membrane pinches in as a new cell wall forms between the two DNA copies, producing two daughter cells. In Amoeba, the nucleus divides first, followed by division of the cytoplasm, producing two daughter amoebae.
A stolon is a horizontal stem that grows above the ground, whereas a rhizome is a horizontal stem that grows below the ground. Both can form new shoots and roots at their nodes.
A bulb is a short underground stem with fleshy leaves. A corm is a swollen underground stem without fleshy leaves; it is covered by dry, scale-like leaves.

Vegetative propagation is asexual reproduction in which a new plant grows from a vegetative part of the parent, such as a root, stem, or leaf. Artificial propagation is vegetative propagation carried out by people using methods such as cuttings, grafting, and layering.

The bacterial DNA replicates, and the two DNA molecules move to opposite sides of the cell. The membrane then pinches inward and a new cell wall forms between them, dividing the cell into two daughter bacteria.

Vegetative propagation is asexual reproduction in which a new plant grows from a vegetative part of the parent, such as a root, stem, or leaf. A stolon is a horizontal stem growing above ground; a rhizome is a horizontal stem growing below ground; a tuber is a fleshy underground stem with buds called eyes; a bulb is a short underground stem with fleshy leaves; and a corm is a swollen underground stem without fleshy leaves. Suckers are shoots arising from the base of a plant or its underground roots. In Bryophyllum, buds along the leaf margins can grow into new plants.
Spores have thick walls that help them tolerate unfavourable conditions and germinate when conditions become favourable. Bacterial endospores can survive even if the original cell dies.

Asexual reproduction generally produces offspring genetically identical to the parent and does not create the variation associated with sexual reproduction. Sexual reproduction involves fusion of male and female gametes and produces variation among offspring and between offspring and their parents.
